0.0.n: Refers to one of two participants, rather than both.

0.1.n: Marks the person receiving the paper.

0.2.n: Names the language used to write the word.

0.3.n: Marks the language used for writing.

0.4.n: Past passive form of 書く; describes the word as something someone wrote.

0.5.n: Refers to an individual vocabulary item written on the paper.

0.6.n: Links 単語 to 紙, describing the paper by the word it contains.

0.7.n: Refers to the sheet bearing the foreign-language word.

0.8.n: Marks the paper as what will be handed out.

0.9.n: Polite form of 配る, used here to announce the next step.

1.0.n: Combines with 片方 to refer to the remaining person in the pair.

1.1.n: With もう, identifies the participant who does not receive the word.

1.2.n: Sets up the other participant as the topic, contrasting them with the first.

1.4.n: Here this is paper for writing, unlike the sheet bearing the word.

1.5.n: Joins the two items provided to the other participant.

1.6.n: A loanword written in katakana, naming the writing tool.

1.7.n: Introduces 紙とペン as the contents of the arrangement described by 形.

1.8.n: Refers to how the activity is set up, not a physical outline.

1.9.n: Marks the resulting arrangement in 形にしてある.

1.10.n: て-form of する plus ある indicates a deliberate arrangement that remains in place.

1.11.n: Gives this setup as the reason for the instructions that follow.

2.0.n: An English loanword referring to the vocabulary item on the paper.

2.1.n: Marks ワード as what the participant has.

2.2.n: Shortened form of 持っている, describing current possession.

2.3.n: Read ほう here; identifies the member of the pair who has the word.

2.4.n: Makes the participant with the word the topic of the instruction.

2.5.n: Used with で to express speaking aloud rather than showing the written word.

2.6.n: Marks the mouth as the means of communicating.

2.7.n: Combines 説明 with する to form a verb.

2.8.n: Presents verbal explanation as one possible way to convey the word.

2.9.n: て-form of する; connects the example activity to the following request.

3.0.n: Modifies 単語 within an embedded question.

3.1.n: Names the vocabulary item the listener needs to identify.

3.2.n: Marks 単語 as the thing that is written.

3.3.n: Shortened 書かれている, combining the passive of 書く with ている to describe the writing on the paper.

3.4.n: Ends the embedded question about what word is written.

3.5.n: Marks the entire question ending in か as the information to convey.

3.6.n: て-form of 伝える plus ください makes a polite request.

4.0.n: Refers to the written symbols making up the word, rather than its meaning.

4.1.n: Marks 文字 as what the other participant should write down.

4.2.n: Combines with に to describe how the characters should be transcribed.

4.3.n: Turns 正確 into a description of how the writing is done.

4.4.n: The connecting form of 書く; joins 取る to make 書き取る, meaning to transcribe.

4.5.n: The ability form of 取る; here it completes 書き取れる, meaning can transcribe.

4.6.n: Combines with に after 書き取れる to introduce the desired outcome.

4.7.n: Completes ように, linking accurate transcription to how the word should be conveyed.

4.8.n: て-form of 伝える plus ほしい expresses what the speaker wants someone else to do.

4.9.n: Shortened の adds an explanatory tone, clarifying the aim of the task.

4.10.n: Makes the explanation polite; it does not mean a separate action here.

4.11.n: Softly invites shared understanding of the instruction.

0.lit: To one person, we will distribute paper with a word written in a foreign language.
0.tip: 書かれた describes 単語: Japanese puts descriptions like written in a foreign language before the noun.

1.lit: As for the other person, since we have arranged it as paper and a pen,
1.tip: してある signals that someone deliberately prepared the setup and it remains ready.

2.lit: As for the person who has the word, by doing things like explaining with their mouth,
2.tip: 持ってる is conversational 持っている; here it means having something, not actively picking it up.

3.lit: Please convey what kind of word is written.
3.tip: かを turns the whole question into the information that someone should convey.

4.lit: We want you to convey it so that they can transcribe the characters accurately, you see.
4.tip: An ability form followed by ように expresses the intended outcome: so that someone can do something.
